name: Seasonal movement
describes: Wood takes up and gives off moisture with the room's humidity and swells and shrinks across the grain, about twice as much tangentially as radially and hardly at all along it. Boards open fine gaps at their joints in a dry winter and close them in summer; plain-sawn boards cup; big timbers check (split) along the grain as they dry, and the checks telegraph through paint as hairline cracks. The trades answer it: pegged, unglued Versailles panels; quarter-sawn boards; hemp laid across the grain in a 地仗 ground.

shrinkage.conditions: green (or saturated) to oven-dry; in service the change follows the moisture content's seasonal swing, a fraction of these

quarterSawn.text: Quarter-sawn boards have less cupping and less shrinkage across the width.

nanmu.text: Nanmu does not react to humidity and temperature much by expansion or contraction; it dries with little splitting or warping.

versaillesPanels.text: Pieces pegged, tenoned and mortised by hand without glue.
versaillesPanels.source: Marc Maison, 'Parquet de Versailles', Architectural antiques resources, https://www.marcmaison.fr/architectural-antiques-resources/parquet-de-versailles (read 2026-09-26)

hempAcrossGrain.text: The hemp is laid perpendicular to the member's grain on the 通灰 and hammered flat.
